channel.title: AD Biomarker Field Brief
channel.description: A curated evidence monitor for Alzheimer disease biomarkers, clinical trials, clinical guidelines, and management updates that may change scientific exchange, diagnosis, treatment, care, or access.

item.title: UK consensus guidance restricts blood testing to clinically suspected AD
item.description: ABN and RCPsych guidance recommends plasma p-tau217 as the preferred blood biomarker, testing only after comprehensive assessment and objective cognitive impairment, and a two-cutoff pathway with CSF or PET follow-up for indeterminate results.

item.title: SynVesT-1 PET did not establish noninferiority to FDG PET
item.description: In 94 patients referred for cognitive-decline imaging, quantitative 18F-SynVesT-1 PET had lower AUC than 18F-FDG PET for AD (0.71 vs 0.81), and the prespecified noninferiority margin was not met.

item.title: AA-2024 nearly doubled CSF-defined biological AD in one clinic
item.description: Among 146 consecutive tertiary-clinic patients, AA-2024 classified 49.3% as biological AD versus 27.4% under AT(N) 2018; all 32 reclassifications moved from non-AD to AD despite lower tau burden and heterogeneous clinical diagnoses.

item.title: Brain-derived enrichment reduced ALS confounding of p-tau217
item.description: In a multicenter serum study, isolating brain-derived tau increased AD-versus-ALS p-tau217 AUC from 0.729 to 0.900; muscle mass spectrometry detected only big-tau p-tau217, identifying a peripheral source of false-positive signal.

item.title: Refrigerated whole blood preserved the Lumipulse ratio for 24 hours
item.description: In 20 participants, the FDA-cleared Lumipulse p-tau217/Aβ42 ratio remained within prespecified stability criteria after refrigerated whole blood was held for 24 hours; 48 hours showed 9.8% mean absolute error and proportional bias.

item.title: CSF p-tau181/Aβ42 shows the strongest PET concordance in meta-analysis
item.description: Across 38 studies and 7,504 participants, CSF p-tau181/Aβ42 had pooled sensitivity 0.920, specificity 0.884 and bivariate AUC 0.955 against amyloid PET, but heterogeneity and publication bias limit direct implementation.

item.title: p-tau217/PET discordance has direction-specific meaning
item.description: Across 1,069 cognitively normal adults, plasma p-tau217-positive/PET-negative and p-tau217-negative/PET-positive profiles carried different biomarker and longitudinal signals, and the p-tau217 operating point changed their interpretation.

item.title: Automated p-tau217 dual cutoffs leave an 11.9% gray zone
item.description: In 135 Taiwanese memory-clinic participants, cohort-derived Roche Elecsys p-tau217 cutoffs below 0.225 and above 0.336 pg/mL classified 88.1% into definitive zones with 95.0% agreement inside those zones.

item.title: Plasma p-tau217 changes etiologic classification in a memory clinic
item.description: In 98 evaluable memory-clinic patients, adding plasma p-tau217 or PrecivityAD2 changed the AD versus non-AD etiologic classification in 37.8% using a 0.18 p-tau217 threshold and 46.9% using a 0.325 threshold.

item.title: Two-stage p-tau217 reflex testing reduces the modeled PET gray zone
item.description: In external validation among 1,644 A4/LEARN participants, a p-tau217 gatekeeper followed by a multimarker reflex model improved gray-zone AUC from 0.719 to 0.793, reduced PET referral from 35.9% to 24.3%, and classified 90.7% without PET.

item.title: Korean registry quantifies real-world lecanemab ARIA and early PET clearance
item.description: Among 663 lecanemab-treated patients at 32 Korean hospitals, ARIA occurred in 16.1%, symptomatic ARIA-E in 0.6%, and baseline superficial siderosis was associated with a 7.45-fold higher hazard of ARIA-E.

item.title: FDA cleared Elecsys pTau181 Plasma as a primary-care rule-out aid
item.description: At 13.1% amyloid-PET prevalence, the single 0.722 pg/mL cutoff produced 92.7% positive agreement, 51.3% negative agreement, 97.9% NPV, and 22.4% PPV in 312 primary-care patients.

item.title: Baseline MRI markers stratify anti-amyloid outcomes and ARIA-H risk
item.description: In a 161-patient real-world anti-amyloid cohort, severe medial-temporal atrophy predicted greater 12-month functional worsening during lecanemab, while baseline microbleeds were associated with a 14-fold higher odds of ARIA-H across lecanemab and donanemab treatment.

item.title: Baseline amyloid burden predicts one-year donanemab PET clearance
item.description: In a TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 post-hoc analysis, lower baseline amyloid was the strongest predictor of reaching less than 24.1 Centiloids at week 52; amyloid-clear and non-clear subgroups had similar CDR-SB slowing, while tau-PET slowing was significant only after clearance.

item.title: Italian intersocietal consensus specifies an anti-amyloid implementation pathway
item.description: Twenty-one Italian scientific societies and patient associations endorsed 36 operational statements that pair trial-aligned MRI eligibility and risk-adapted ARIA monitoring with a stepwise confirmation pathway using plasma biomarkers, automated CSF assays and amyloid PET.

item.title: An anatomical phantom exposes material bias in uncorrected amyloid-PET quantification
item.description: Across simulated gray-to-white matter ratios, uncorrected amyloid-PET measures had mean absolute inaccuracies of 14.1% for tissue ratio and 19.8% for SUVR; partial-volume correction reduced them as low as 6.1% and 7.6%, with modified 3-compartment and GTM methods performing best.

item.title: Real-world lecanemab PET monitoring reveals visual-quantitative discordance
item.description: In 38 amyloid-PET-positive patients treated for 6–8 months, amyloid burden fell by 29.39±22.31 Centiloids, but visual and quantitative response agreement was poor to fair (κ 0.205–0.253), supporting explicit Centiloid quantification for serial monitoring rather than visual interpretation alone.

item.title: Autopsy validation shows late-stage flortaucipir uptake differs across primary cortex
item.description: Among 155 autopsy-confirmed Alzheimer cases, flortaucipir uptake in primary isocortices began at Braak stage V, with visual and auditory regions increasing earlier and faster than motor and somatosensory regions.

item.title: Low-intensity resource referral misses its caregiver self-efficacy endpoint
item.description: In a single-blind randomized trial, CommunityRx-Dementia did not improve 12-month caregiver self-efficacy or most prespecified outcomes among 133 caregivers with health-related social risks, although emergency-department use was lower (IRR 0.41, 95% CI 0.19-0.90).

item.title: Quantitative MRI plus local language models drafts neurodegenerative reports
item.description: In 192 ADNI cases, an automated MRI-to-report pipeline achieved 77.6%-97.9% accuracy for CSF-space findings and 91.7%-97.4% agreement within one grade on ordinal visual scales, but strict scale agreement was only 27.1%-57.8% and no clinical utility was tested.

item.title: Sequential Lumipulse testing reduced the p-tau217 indeterminate zone
item.description: In 562 consecutive memory-clinic patients, using the p-tau217/Aβ42 ratio only after an intermediate p-tau217 result reduced indeterminate classifications from 17.8% to 12.3% and was estimated to spare 56 confirmatory CSF or amyloid-PET tests per 1,000 patients.

item.title: Plasma p-tau217 did not identify amyloid clearance after donanemab
item.description: Among donanemab-treated TRAILBLAZER-ALZ 2 participants, plasma p-tau217 had an AUC of 0.61 at week 52 for detecting PET amyloid below 24.1 Centiloids, so the blood marker could not substitute for PET when determining individual treatment-related amyloid clearance.

item.title: PET, CSF, and plasma discordance was modeled as probability, not test error
item.description: In 320 ADNI participants, PET and CSF classifications disagreed in 12% even when obtained within seven days; a latent-class model used plasma Aβ42/40 or %p-tau217 to refine uncertainty rather than declaring either PET or CSF an infallible reference.

item.title: Structured tau-PET reading review translates consensus into reporting practice
item.description: This evidence-based review lays out a structured approach to tau-PET visual interpretation, validated scoring systems, quantitative thresholds, and standardized reporting—an implementation-focused publication that the prior original-study-heavy criteria could miss.

item.title: Longitudinal p-tau217 categories remain stable and stratify progression risk
item.description: Across 2,117 participants in three cohorts, baseline assay-specific p-tau217 cutoffs retained 86%-95% accuracy for amyloid-PET status over as long as five years; positive classifications were usually stable, while intermediate results converted to positive more often than negative results.

item.title: M-ACE supports rapid functional staging across the AD continuum
item.description: In 1,834 consecutive patients, the Mini-Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination closely tracked the full ACE-III (ρ=0.822), outperformed MMSE at the subjective-decline-to-MCI transition and yielded stage-specific cutoffs, but retrospective FAST-based classification does not establish etiologic Alzheimer diagnosis or treatment eligibility.

item.title: Model quantifies value lost when anti-amyloid treatment is delayed
item.description: A U.S. microsimulation projected $104,885 in gross lifetime societal value per treated person and 32% more value when anti-amyloid treatment began two years earlier, but these are model-based gross benefits that exclude drug, screening and monitoring costs.

item.title: Sweet-tooth preference tracks with higher dementia risk
item.description: In a prospective UK Biobank analysis, a sweet-tooth preference profile was associated with 79% higher all-cause dementia risk, 62% higher Alzheimer disease risk and 202% higher vascular-dementia risk than a health-aligned profile; the observational design does not show that changing preference prevents dementia.

item.title: Earlier blood-biomarker disclosure raises certainty and changes care
item.description: In the 220-person PLASMAR randomized trial, disclosing plasma p-tau217 and NfL at three rather than nine months increased very high-confidence etiologic diagnoses from 4.6% to 50.0% and advanced several management decisions without worse anxiety, depression or quality of life.

item.title: Clinical context helps explain definite-zone p-tau217 discordance
item.description: Among 706 Mayo Clinic patients with plasma p-tau217 outside the intermediate zone and confirmatory amyloid PET and/or CSF, 60 (8.5%) were discordant: false negatives were more common than false positives (5.6% vs 2.8%; p=0.007), with disease stage, kidney function, body mass index and obstructive sleep apnea associated with discordance patterns.
